topic: volumes with known cross sections and cylindrical shells
subtitle: Volumes by integrating a known cross-sectional area, volumes by cylindrical shells, and choosing between the two

problems.note: Base bounded by y = x, y = 0, x = 4; square cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis.

traps.desc: found the area of the base region instead of the volume of the solid

problems.note: Base bounded by y = sqrt(x), y = 0, x = 9; semicircular cross sections with the diameter on the base.

traps.desc: treated the height of the base as the RADIUS of the semicircle instead of its diameter

problems.note: Region under y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 3 revolved about the y-axis, by shells.

traps.desc: left out the 2*pi circumference factor and integrated only radius times height

problems.note: Base is the half-disc under y = sqrt(16 - x^2); square cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis.

traps.desc: integrated the side length instead of its square, so the cross-sectional area was wrong

problems.note: Region under y = sqrt(x) from x = 0 to x = 4 revolved about the y-axis, by shells.

traps.desc: used discs about the x-axis instead of shells about the y-axis

problems.note: Base bounded by y = 4 - x^2 and the x-axis; equilateral-triangle cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis.
Decimal form of the same volume, to two decimal places.

traps.desc: used the square-cross-section area instead of the equilateral-triangle area

problems.note: Limits of integration: where y = 2x meets y = x^2.
Shell height is the vertical gap between the two curves.

traps.desc: used only the upper curve as the shell height and ignored the lower boundary

problems.note: Region bounded by y = x^2, x = 0 and y = 4 revolved about the y-axis; shells in x avoid solving for x in terms of y.

problems.desc: Written justification for choosing shells in x over washers in y for this region — open reasoning, read by hand.
